title: Extraction and Measurement of Polyphosphate and Inorganic Phosphorus from Microalgae Samples
author: Yingyu Hu
materials: Flash freeze filters and stored at -80 °C
Tris buffer 20 mM pH 7.0 Budget: About 250 mL per four samples
In a 1 L volumetric flask, top 20 mL 1 M pH 7.0 Tris buffer to 1 L with MilliQ
Store at Room temperature
PolyP primary standard stock
Weigh one glass pellet of polyP (45) and write down the weight. Microbalance (Cubis series, Sartorius, MSE6.6S-000-DM)
Transfer the pellet into a 100 mL graduated cylinder.
Dilute to 100 mL with Tris 20 mM pH 7.0
Aliquot primary stock into 10~50 uL per microtube with Stepper and store at -20 °C
PolyP secondary standard stock If the pellet is far more than 10 mg, dilute primary to secondary to bring down the concentration before preparing working standard
Proteinase K 20 mg/ml
Add 25 mL MilliQ directly into the original package of Proteinase K, vortex to mix
Aliquot 700 uL to microtubes and keep frozen at -20 °C
DAPI primary stock 14.3 mM Add 2 mL MilliQ directly into the original package and keep frozen at -20 °C
Read fluorescence: excitation at 410 nm and emission at 550 nm Varioskan LUX Multimode Microplate Reader (Thermo Fisher, VL0L00D0)
In Set S, add 36 µL Proteinase
Thaw proteinase (~700uL)
In Set B, add 30 µL Proteinase
Calculation
Preliminary extraction efficiency test

2.5 % ammonium molybdate reagent: Weigh 0.25 g ammonium molybdate in a Falcon tube and top to 10 g with MilliQ water. Cap and shake until totally dissolved. Ammonium molybdate Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #09878-100G (CAS: 12054-85-2)

10 % ascorbic acid reagent: Weigh 1 g ascorbic acid in a Falcon tube and top to 10 g with MilliQ water; Cap and shake until all dissolved. Ascorbic acid Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #A5960-100G (CAS: 50-81-7)
Preheat incubator/shaker to 37 °C

steps.title: Collect and Prepare Microalgae Samples
steps.instruction: Filter microalgae in liquid media onto GF/F or PC filters using gentle vacuum pressure (130 mmHg) with stainless steel blunt-end filter forceps (Millipore, XX6200006P).

substeps.instruction: Rinse the sample with filtered saline (no nutrients).
Place sample filters in cryogenic vials.
Filter the same volume of blank media (without cells) through GF/F or PC filter as a blank.
Freeze dry samples using a FreeZone® 2.5 L Benchtop Freeze Dryer (Labconco®, 700202000).

steps.title: Perform Preliminary Extraction Efficiency Test
steps.instruction: Determine the optimal number of extractions (N) required to stop the decrease of fluorescence in stained extracts.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a boiling bath using VWR® Advanced Hot Plates (VWR, 97042-658) with 20 mm Hollow PP Ball Bath Covers (Cole-Parmer, UZ-06821-04) and a Simport MultiRack™ (CA48648-606).
Transfer sample into 10 mL disposable glass screw-cap centrifuge tubes (Corning®, 99502-10).
Add 4 mL Tris buffer (20 mM, pH 7.0), vortex, and sonicate.
Incubate in the boiling bath for 5 minutes, ensuring the tube rack is centered and covered with PP balls so the Tris solution boils.
Sonicate again.

Vortex and transfer the extract to a 15 mL Falcon tube using a soda-lime glass Pasteur pipet (Fisherbrand, 13-678-6A); gently lift the filter and press the extract out without pushing the filter to the bottom.
Repeat the extraction process up to 15 times.
Centrifuge the extract at 3200 rpm at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Load 200 µL of supernatant from each extract into a 96-well black microplate (Greiner Bio-One, 655076) using forward pipetting; use 20 mM pH 7.0 Tris buffer as a blank.
Prepare 100 µM DAPI working solution by diluting 12.6 µL of 14.3 mM DAPI stock with 1800 µL MilliQ in a foil-wrapped microtube and vortex.
In a dimmed room with red light, add 24 µL of 100 µM DAPI to each sample.
Cover the plate with a lid and black vinyl film (VWR, 89087-692).
Shake at room temperature for 7 minutes.

Plot fluorescence intensity vs. extraction number. Identify the stationary point (N) where fluorescence stops decreasing. If RFU(15)-RFU(Tris) > 1, perform five additional extractions and measure again.

steps.title: Process Enzyme Treated Extracts
steps.instruction: Combine and treat the extracts from 1 to N with enzymes to remove nucleic acids.

substeps.instruction: Combine extractions 1 through N into a Falcon tube (or beaker if volume > 50 mL), including debris.
Mix the combined extract and transfer 12 mL into a 15 mL Falcon tube; centrifuge at 3200 rpm at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Transfer 1.8 mL of supernatant to a 2 mL tube (Set S) in triplicate (S1a, S1b, S1c, etc.).
Transfer 1.5 mL of supernatant into a 2 mL tube (Set B) for blanks; duplicate (B1a, B1b, etc.).
In Set S, add 18 µL RNase and 18 µL DNase. To avoid waste and residue, use the same tip to draw and dispense the RNase solution back into the vial three times before replacing the tip.
In Set B, add 15 µL RNase and 15 µL DNase.
Incubate at 37 °C in a shaking incubator (Corning® LSE™, 6753), starting the timer once the temperature reaches 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Standard Amended Extracts
steps.instruction: Create amended samples using a PolyP working standard to calibrate measurements.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 7.6 µM PolyP working standard by diluting PolyP (45) stock with 20 mM pH 7.0 Tris buffer (Total volume = 160 X N µL, where N = sample number; FW=10600; 110 mol PO3 per mol PolyP (45)).
Transfer 840 µL of enzyme-treated extract (1~N) into 2 mL tubes (Set A) using forward pipetting (aspire/dispense 3 times to mix).
Add 160 µL of 7.6 µM PolyP working standard to the 840 µL extract and vortex.

steps.title: Measure PolyP Fluorescence
steps.instruction: Measure the fluorescence of blanks, samples, and amended samples.

substeps.instruction: Load 200 µL of blanks (B), samples (S), and amended samples (A) into a microplate using reverse pipetting.
In a dimmed room with red light, add 24 µL of 100 µM DAPI working solution to all wells except those labeled (UN) using forward pipetting.
Cover the plate with a lid and black film.
Shake at room temperature for 7 minutes.
Perform final measurement: shake for 1 min (continuous, 600 rpm, high force); excitation at 410 nm, emission at 550 nm, measurement time 300 ms, excitation bandwidth 5 nm.

steps.title: Measure Inorganic Phosphorus (Pi)
steps.instruction: Quantify inorganic phosphorus using a molybdate-ascorbic acid assay.

substeps.instruction: Prepare KH2PO4 primary standard stock (≈ 1 mM): Dry ~1 g KH2PO4 (ACP Chemicals #P-4550) at 110 °C for 2 hours, cool in a vacuum desiccator, and dissolve ~0.136 g in 1 L MilliQ water using a volumetric flask. Store in the fridge.
Prepare a dilution series (S1-S8) using the stock and MilliQ water (e.g., S1: 0 µL stock/1000 µL MilliQ; S8: 200 µL stock/800 µL MilliQ).
Transfer 500 µL of each standard working solution to 2 mL microtubes.
Transfer 500 µL of supernatant from each extract (1-1, 1-2... N) to 2 mL microtubes and warm to room temperature.
Prepare 6 N (3 M) sulfuric acid by adding 1 part 18 M concentrated sulfuric acid to 5 parts MilliQ water.

Prepare molybdate-ascorbic reagent: Total volume = (0.5 mL) X (#standards + #samples + #blanks). Mix in a Falcon tube: 2 parts MilliQ, 1 part 6N sulfuric acid, 1 part 2.5% ammonium molybdate, and 1 part 10% ascorbic acid.
Add 500 µL of the reagent to each standard, sample, and blank using Finntip Stepper Tips (5 mL); wipe the outside of the tip before dispensing.
Vortex each tube and incubate at 37 °C for 3 hours while shaking at 200 rpm.
Load 250 µL of reactant from each tube into a microplate in duplicate.
Read plate at 820 nm: shake 5s (continuous, 600 rpm, high force), measurement time 100 ms.

steps.title: Calculate Phosphorus Concentrations
steps.instruction: Process absorbance data to determine orthophosphate and polyP concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Subtract average blank standard absorbance from all other standard working solutions.
Subtract average blank sample (blank filter) absorbance from all individual samples.
Create a standard curve (blank-corrected 820 nm absorbance vs. concentration in µM) to determine orthophosphate concentration of unknown samples.
